<!-- no-figure: a one-line inequality -->
#### A cubic dominates a quadratic

Let $f(n) = n^2$ and $g(n) = n^3$, and let $\epsilon > 0$.
Choose an integer $n_0 \ge 1/\epsilon$.
For every $n \ge n_0$ we have $1/n \le 1/n_0 \le \epsilon$, so

$$
f(n) = n^2 = \frac{1}{n} \, n^3 \le \epsilon \, n^3 = \epsilon \, g(n).
$$

Hence $n^2 = o(n^3)$ by @def-little-o, so $n^3$ dominates $n^2$.

:::
